latest_release.name: v12.6.3
latest_release.body:
## v12.6.3 (2026-11-26)

#### Notable changes

**Testing**
* `Test.createTestingModule()` accepts the `instrument` option, like `NestFactory.create()`. Its `instanceDecorator` decorates the module's providers, overridden ones included, and the applications and microservices created from the module use it unless their own options set one. Tests can now run an app instrumented as it is in production. With NestJS Observe, for example, gateway tests no longer log that the `instrument` option is missing – [#18743](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18743)
* Instances that an application context creates through `resolve()` (request-scoped and transient providers) are passed to the `instrument` instance decorator, in a testing module and in `NestFactory.createApplicationContext()` – [#18743](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18743)

**Behaviour changes**
* Route conflict detection compares paths the way the router matches them. On Express, which matches paths in any case, `GET /users` and `GET /Users` are reported as the same route, so `duplicate: 'error'` aborts bootstrap. The same holds on Fastify with `caseSensitive: false`. Nothing changes where the router is case-sensitive: Fastify by default, the Node adapter, and Express with `case sensitive routing` enabled – [#18721](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18721)
* A path excluded without a version, in `MiddlewareConsumer.exclude()` or in the `exclude` option of `enableCsrfProtection()`, also covers the routes of the default version(s), as `forRoutes()` does – [#18601](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18601)
* `@Body('key')` with a falsy primitive body (`""`, `0`, `false`) yields `undefined`, like any other primitive body. It used to receive the whole body – [#18720](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18720)
* `ParseDatePipe` rejects a day past the end of its month in a numeric date without a year (`2/30`, `4/31`; as in `new Date()`, such a date is in 2001, so `2/29` is rejected too), and in a year-first month-name date after a weekday (`Thu 2024 Sept 31`) – [#18724](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18724), [#18727](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18727)
* `GrpcExceptionFilter` logs an exception that isn't an `RpcException` before answering `UNKNOWN`, as `BaseRpcExceptionFilter` does. It used to answer without a trace on the server – [#18722](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18722)
* Security headers: an `undefined` entry in `referrerPolicy.policy` is rejected like any other invalid value – [#18729](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18729)

**Performance**
* The 404 that Nest throws for an unmatched route is created without a stack trace. Server CPU time per 404 drops by 28 to 29% on Express, Fastify and Node (21.9 µs to 15.5 µs on Express) – [#18730](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18730)

**Fastify**
* `httpAdapter.render()` works on the raw response that middleware and their exception filters receive. It used to throw `response.view is not a function` – [#18719](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18719)
* `app.listen(port, host, backlog)` passes the backlog to Fastify. It used to be passed as the callback – [#18736](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18736)
* A `StreamableFile` sent with a 304 status is not read, and the 304 goes out without a body – [#18723](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18723)
* A request aborted by the client mid-body becomes a 400 `HttpException`, instead of an unexpected error – [#18726](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18726)

**WebSockets**
* Gateways whose `path` is spelled differently (`events`, `/events/`) share one server. The second one used to get its own server, which never received a client – [#18728](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18728)
* With gateways that share a socket.io server, each disconnect is handled once, also when a `handleDisconnect` hook disconnects other clients – [#18745](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18745)

#### Features
* `testing`, `core`
